utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for those answers. Any -- have the questions of the Bench triggered any need for further questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I have just one question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just one question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm looking at the clock. I'm guilty, myself, Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I will be very short.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Further cross-examination by Mr. Mikulicic:

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Cetina, Judge Kinis asked you about such situations in which policemen, when coming across a corpse, notified sanitation teams. It is true and correct - is it not? - that there was always a crime technician who would be part of such a group of people?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And this scene-of-crime officer, as a trained policeman, was able to ascertain whether there were any grounds to believe that a murder was involved when studying such a corpse?

utterances.speaker: IVICA CETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your answers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: By the way, Mr. Mikulicic, that is not what Judge Kinis put to the witness, as a matter of fact, but -- and I verified that with him. That is, upon receiving information about dead bodies, sending sanitation immediately, not finding a body on your way. But let's leave that alone for the time being. Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Just to let the Chamber know, we have the translation of that Brgud document, while the witness is here. We can show it via Sanction. Otherwise, we can tender it Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would like to have a look at it. I don't know whether it is long or short.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It's one page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One page. Could it be shown, and I'm aware that ... Not necessarily to be shown to the witness yet, but let's see whether it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: We have to show it via Sanction, Mr. President, because it is not in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that would, then, be under our ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: While we're waiting, Your Honour, the bar table matter that I referred to yesterday, I've used some of those documents now so it's -- they've come off the bar table.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if you, then, could please. I'm a bit worried about all those assisting us, Mr. Kay, Friday, five minutes. If it is an administrative matter, that you should take them out from your bar table list, then we can deal with that. Unless there is anything urgent to be done in court at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It's just that two documents remain, and they can be made exhibits, to deal with it. Everything else has been dealt with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, Ms. Mahindaratne, are you aware of which documents we're talking about?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, during the break I reviewed them, and I have no objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections. That would be, Mr. Kay ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 65 ter 984. If that could be made an exhibit, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit D1770.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 65 ter 147. If that could be made an exhibit, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit D1771.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Let's -- this Sanction document. I don't see anything on my screen but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you just give me a second to read it. Yes, that certainly fills in. I don't think that the witness could -- could give us further information about that. But at least it gives more complete picture of the sequence of events. May -- would you like to bar table this -- or would you like to have this document -- then we'll deal with it in the technical matter because it's not yet uploaded. But, Mr. Kay, is it something you'd --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We can bar table it, and we will deal with it as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Mr. Cetina, on the assumption that there are no further questions from Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President, I don't have any questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then this concludes your testimony in this court. I would like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague. We're glad that we can release you still on Friday, so that you don't have to stay over the weekend. I would like to thank you for having answered the questions that were put to you by the parties and the questions that were put to you by the Bench. And I wish you a safe trip home again. We adjourn, and we will resume on Monday, the 2nd of November, 9.00, Courtroom III.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 2nd day of November, 2009, at 9.00 a.m. 25
